title: Multiple adhesion molecules act together in oligodendrocyte-mediated axonal selection and myelin formation
experiments_summary: The study employed zebrafish as the primary model organism. CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing was used to generate a cadm4 knockout (KO) line via an 8-bp deletion in exon 4, which was then outcrossed with previously established mag−/− and cntn1b−/−mag−/− lines to produce cadm4−/−mag−/− double KO (dKO) and cadm4−/−cntn1b−/−mag−/− triple KO (CCM−/− tKO) fish. Genotyping was performed via PCR and restriction enzyme digestion. Knockout confirmation and expression of cadm family members (cadm1a, cadm1b, cadm2a, cadm2b, cadm3) were assessed by qPCR using the ΔΔCt method on RNA isolated from 8 dpf larvae. Fusion proteins (olig1:cadm4-EGFP, olig1:mag-EGFP, huC:cadm3-EGFP, UAS:caspr-EYFP, myrf:EGFP-CAAX) were generated by Gateway cloning and introduced by microinjection at the one-cell stage for sparse or mosaic labeling. Localization of Cadm4, MAG, Cadm3, and Caspr was assessed by single time-point and time-lapse confocal microscopy using a Leica TCS SP8 with resonant scanner and water-immersion objective, with larvae mounted in low-melting agarose. Single time-point confocal imaging of stable transgenic lines (mbp:EGFP-CAAX, sox10:mRFP) was performed at 4 dpf and 8 dpf to quantify myelinated area, OL process number, sheath number and length, myelin stubs, ectopic cell body ensheathments, and OPC/OL cell counts. In vivo time-lapse imaging over 13 hours starting at 2.5 dpf was used to track individual OL differentiation, myelin sheath initiation, stabilization, and retraction, as well as OL cell death, in wild-type, dKO, and tKO fish. For ultrastructural analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was performed on spinal cord cross-sections from 8 dpf larvae and 2.5-month-old adult fish, prepared by chemical fixation, osmium tetroxide post-fixation, en bloc staining, ethanol dehydration, and LX112 embedding, followed by sectioning at 100 nm and imaging on a Zeiss Crossbeam 340. SEM quantifications included total myelinated axon density, compaction state, multi-myelin profiles, myelin outfoldings, axonal diameter distributions, percentage of myelinated axons below 1 µm, mean diameter of the 30 largest axons, and Mauthner axon diameter. All image quantifications were performed in FIJI, IMARIS, and QuPath, and statistical analyses used one-way ANOVA, Kruskal–Wallis, or Brown–Forsythe/Welch ANOVA with appropriate post-hoc tests in GraphPad Prism.
